remaining_warnings: MCP validation N/A for this change: app/db/models/shop.model.ts is a backend Sequelize model fix with no Admin GraphQL, Polaris web-component, or Liquid/theme surface -- no validate_graphql_codeblocks / validate_component_codeblocks / validate_theme call applies. Stated explicitly per rule 8, not silently skipped.

KNOWN CHECKER GAP (disclosed, not worked around): tools/scripts/check-dev-handoff.py's strict decision semantics require overall_status=VALID to carry >=1 validations (`reject("overall_status VALID but no validations recorded")`) -- it has no distinct path for a legitimately MCP-not-applicable backend fix, only VALID/INVALID/BLOCKED, and BLOCKED means 'must NOT proceed', which would misrepresent this fix (fully implemented, live-verified, all four gates passing). Ran the checker manually against this exact evidence file and got that rejection, confirming the gap is real, not hypothetical. Per this agent's own operating rule ('For generic Node.js, Sequelize, or PostgreSQL work with no Shopify-specific API or UI impact, MCP validation is not mandatory -- say so explicitly in the handoff'), overall_status is kept VALID and validations is honestly left empty rather than fabricating a fake validation entry to force the checker to pass. Flagged for the orchestrator/human to account for when running the checker on this handoff -- this is a checker-tooling limitation, not a defect in the fix or its evidence.

run-gates.py (tools/scripts/run-gates.py) still fails on this Windows environment with subprocess.run(['npm',...], shell=False) -> [WinError 2] (npm.cmd cannot be exec'd without shell resolution) -- same cross-platform gap disclosed every round since G4-sprint-1.1. Gate logs in this evidence directory were produced by a manual equivalent with the identical argv/command and __GATE_EXIT__-marker contract, not by run-gates.py itself. Not something this developer agent is authorized to fix unprompted (no command given for the plugin script itself).

Environment observation, NOT a code defect: this session's DATABASE_URL-backed Neon Postgres briefly showed an inconsistent information_schema.tables read immediately after a cold connection (a fresh query reported only the SequelizeMeta table, while a follow-up query moments later, and every query thereafter, correctly showed all 9 application tables including shop). Reproduced the same result twice with different query shapes before it self-resolved; consistent with Neon serverless compute cold-start/catalog-cache lag on a freshly-woken connection, not with anything in this repo's code or migrations. Did not affect the live-evidence run below (run after the DB had settled, confirmed via an independent read-back at every step). Flagged for awareness only -- not investigated further, out of scope for this commanded fix.

db/config/config.cjs eagerly evaluates ALL THREE environment blocks (development/test/production) as one object literal at require-time, so migrationUrl('production')'s strict 'DIRECT_DATABASE_URL is required' throw fires even when running migrations for development/test -- this blocked `npm run db:migrate` in this environment (.env has no DIRECT_DATABASE_URL set) until worked around with a session-only inline env var (DIRECT_DATABASE_URL=$DATABASE_URL, not written to .env, matching the precedent in dev-evidence/g4-sprint-1.1-live-evidence-v4's inline-env-var-for-this-session-only pattern). This is a real, reproducible local-dev friction bug in db/config/config.cjs, but it is NOT part of this sprint's commanded fix (ShopModel.installedAt only) and was not touched -- flagged for a human fix-decision, not fixed under the no-auto-fix rule.
live_store_items: This fix was verified against a real Neon Postgres dev database, not a live Shopify dev store -- no real token-exchange handshake (real session-token JWT) was exercised, since that requires a live embedded-admin request this sandbox cannot produce. Step 4 of live-evidence.ts exercises the SAME PostgreSQLSessionStorage instance app/shopify.server.ts wires up directly, mirroring auth.$.tsx's loader body line for line, which is the closest verification possible without a real store. Confirming the full real token-exchange install (a genuinely new merchant installing from the Partner Dashboard listing / a fresh dev store) against this fix remains a live-store item for the next dev-store-connected verification round.
